heading: Compromise
lead: The Attorney General or his designee may arbitrate, compromise, or settle any claim cognizable under section 1346(b) of this title, after the commencement of an action thereon.

notes.heading: Historical and Revision Notes
notes.text: Based on title 28, U.S.C., 1940 ed., § 934 (Aug. 2, 1946, ch. 753, § 413, 60 Stat. 845). Changes were made in phraseology.

notes.heading: Senate Revision Amendment
notes.text: This section was renumbered “2676” by Senate amendment. See 80th Congress Senate Report No. 1559.

notes.heading: Amendments
notes.text: 1966—Pub. L. 89–506 struck out provision requiring that approval of court be obtained before Attorney General could arbitrate, compromise, or settle a claim after commencement of an action thereon.

notes.heading: Effective Date of 1966 Amendment
notes.text: Amendment by Pub. L. 89–506 applicable to claims accruing six months or more after July 18, 1966, see section 10 of Pub. L. 89–506, set out as a note under section 2672 of this title.
